stages.label: The post at the edge of the sea
Just the feeling of the breath

spans.quote: Sit in a half-lotus position, right leg on top of the left leg, your hands placed palm-up on your lap, right hand on top of the left.

instructions.object: half-lotus, right leg on the left; hands palm-up in the lap, right hand on the left

spans.quote: Keep your body straight and your mind on the task before you.

instructions.object: body straight; mind on the task

spans.quote: Raise your hands in respect, palm-to-palm in front of the heart, and think of the qualities of the Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha

instructions.object: qualities of the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha
instructions.gesture: palms together in front of the heart

spans.quote: Buddho me nātho—The Buddha is my mainstay.
Dhammo me nātho—The Dhamma is my mainstay.
Saṅgho me nātho—The Sangha is my mainstay.

instructions.object: Buddho me nātho · Dhammo me nātho · Saṅgho me nātho
instructions.note: Pali shown on screen as quote lines, not spoken by TTS (pronunciation).

spans.quote: Then repeat in your mind, buddho, buddho; dhammo, dhammo; saṅgho, saṅgho.
Return your hands to your lap and repeat one word, buddho, three times in your mind.
Then think of the in-and-out breath, counting the breaths in pairs.
First think bud- with the in-breath, dho with the out, ten times.
Then begin again, thinking buddho with the in-breath, buddho with the out, seven times.
As the breath goes in and out once, think buddho once, five times.
As the breath goes in and out once, think buddho three times.
Do this for three in-and-out breaths.
Now you can stop counting the breaths, and simply think bud- with the in-breath and dho with the out.
Let the breath be relaxed and natural.
Keep your mind perfectly still, focused on the breath as it comes in and out of the nostrils.

locus.note: “the nostrils” drawn at the grammar's tip-of-the-nose locus (the nostrils sit there)

spans.quote: When the breath goes out, don’t send the mind out after it.
When the breath comes in, don’t let the mind follow it in.

warnings: don't follow the breath out or in with the mind

spans.quote: Let your awareness be broad, cheerful, and open.
Don’t force the mind too much.
Relax.
Pretend that you’re breathing out in the wide open air.
Keep the mind still, like a post at the edge of the sea.
When the water rises, the post doesn’t rise with it; when the water ebbs, the post doesn’t sink.
When you’ve reached this level of stillness, you can stop thinking buddho.

conditions: when the mind has reached this level of stillness

spans.quote: Simply be aware of the feeling of the breath.
Then slowly bring your attention inward, focusing it on the various aspects of the breath
the important aspects that can give rise to intuitive powers of various kinds

instructions.intent: the bases of the breath are said to give rise to intuitive powers
instructions.exclude_reason: claims of supernormal powers: kept as orientation (info card / Q&A with the source), never narrated as a promise

spans.quote: The First Base: Center the mind on the tip of the nose and then slowly move it to the middle of the forehead, the Second Base.
Keep your awareness broad.
Let the mind rest for a moment at the forehead and then bring it back to the nose.
Keep moving it back and forth between the nose and the forehead—like a person climbing up and down a mountain—seven times.
Then let it settle at the forehead.
Don’t let it go back to the nose.

warnings: don't go back to the nose

spans.quote: From here, let it move to the Third Base, the middle of the top of the head, and let it settle there for a moment.
Keep your awareness broad.
Inhale the breath at that spot, let it spread throughout the head for a moment, and then return the mind to the middle of the forehead.
Move the mind back and forth between the forehead and the top of the head seven times, finally letting it rest on the top of the head.
Then bring it into the Fourth Base, the middle of the brain.
Let it be still for a moment and then bring it back out to the top of the head.

locus.note: “the middle of the brain” drawn at the grammar's middle-of-the-head locus

spans.quote: Keep moving it back and forth between these two spots, finally letting it settle in the middle of the brain.

locus.note: “these two spots” = the top of the head and the middle of the brain (p7.s1–s2)

spans.quote: Keep your awareness broad.
Let the refined breath in the brain spread to the lower parts of the body.
When you reach this point you may find that the breath starts giving rise to various signs (nimitta), such as seeing or feeling hot, cold, or tingling sensations in the head.
You may see a pale, murky vapor or your own skull.

conditions: signs (nimitta) appear: heat, cold or tingling in the head; a pale vapour; the skull
instructions.exclude_reason: conditional on what the meditator experiences; handled by the Ask layer (preloaded answer + action), not narrated to everyone

spans.quote: Even so, don’t let yourself be affected by whatever appears.
If you don’t want the nimitta to appear, breathe deep and long, down into the heart, and it will immediately go away.

conditions: a sign appears and you don't want it

locus.note: “down into the heart” drawn at the middle of the chest

warnings: don't let yourself be affected by whatever appears

spans.quote: When you see that a nimitta has appeared, mindfully focus your awareness on it—but be sure to focus on only one at a time, choosing whichever one is most comfortable.
Once you’ve got hold of it, expand it so that it’s as large as your head.
When you have this white light as large as the head, bring it down to The Fifth Base, the center of the chest.
Once it’s firmly settled, let it spread out to fill the chest.

Make this breath as white and as bright as possible, and then let both the breath and the light spread throughout the body, out to every pore, until different parts of the body appear on their own as pictures.

instructions.exclude_reason: work with a light sign is conditional on it appearing and is the part Ajaan Lee says to study with a skilled teacher (p12.s5); never scripted, so nobody is pushed to produce lights

spans.quote: If you don’t want the pictures, take two or three long breaths and they’ll disappear.

conditions: pictures of the body appear and you don't want them

spans.quote: Keep your awareness still and expansive.

conditions.note: in the text this follows the light sign; used here for the breath alone

spans.quote: Keep it intent on a single preoccupation, the refined breath, letting this refined breath suffuse the entire body.
The body will be light, like fluff.
The mind will be rested and refreshed—supple, solitary, and self-contained.

instructions.intent: results Ajaan Lee describes when this point is reached
instructions.exclude_reason: an outcome, not an instruction: used in the Ask answer to 'how do I know it's working?' as his description, never promised

spans.quote: To become thoroughly expert you should, if possible, study directly with someone who has practiced and is skilled in these matters

instructions.exclude_reason: goes to facets.needs_teacher_note and the info card

spans.quote: Most people will find that Method 2, which follows, is easier and more relaxing than Method 1, outlined above.

instructions.exclude_reason: goes to safety.alternatives and the start card

spans.quote: If you suffer from frequent headaches or nervous problems, don’t focus on any spot above the base of the throat.

warnings: don't focus on any spot above the base of the throat

applies_to.note: stated in Method 2 for its resting spots; we apply it to Method 1's head bases (Bases 2–4)

instructions.exclude_reason: becomes the beginner form (skip the head bases) and a start-card contraindication

coverage_rules.reason: knowledge/insight teaching after the session (mundane and transcendent knowledge, five summary steps): orientation for the Theory tab, not timed instructions
a claim about the white nimitta's effects (cleansing the blood): not narrated
nimitta handling inside the light work (i38 scope)
other chapter; only p23.s1 (headache caution) is used
